profile.summary: Prior purchases emphasize material, comfort, fit, durability; ratings are usually positive.

messages: hey, i need new scrub pants for work - men's, cargo style if you have them. honestly the big thing is the fabric, it's gotta be that poly cotton blend that survives being washed every single day.
like i said, poly-cotton. my last pair was a 65/35 poplin and it held up for years, so something in that ballpark. definitely not 100% cotton, that stuff wrinkles like crazy.
pockets mostly. i carry a phone, shears and a couple of pens, so the more cargo pockets the better. oh and a real zipper fly - the drawstring-only ones drive me nuts.
eh, no strong preference on color really. whatever's standard for a hospital.
traditional fit, nothing skinny. natural rise, tapered leg, and an elastic waistband with a drawstring tie is ideal.
i'm a large, sometimes an XL depending on the brand. regular inseam, i'm about 5'10".
hospital floor shifts, twelve hours on my feet. i also wear them for prep work in the kitchen at home, so they need to take a beating and wash out.
cheap-ish, under $25 a pair. around twenty bucks would be perfect since i need three of them.
i don't have a strong preference for brand, honestly. cherokee has been fine but whatever lasts.
ok fine - cherokee workwear if you've got it, that's what my unit issues. style 4000 i think.
